[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]A COUNTRY THAT NEVER DECLARES WAR[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Los Vales has never declared a war abroad. Its corporations have fought in almost all of them. The rule, written down for the first time after the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832728][color=#7FDBFF]Strait War[/color][/url][color=white], is simple: the State stays neutral, and everything else is for sale.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE WARS AT A GLANCE[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Nine wars in seventy years, and Los Vales declared none of them.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE SOUTHERN CARTEL WAR (2018–2021)[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]While the United States fell apart, the cartels of Mexico and Central America rose against governments that had lost their northern ally. In 2019 they besieged Monterrey for five months; in 2020 the fighting reached the capitals of three countries. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]ArmaTech[/color][/url][color=white] armed the armies and the cartels at the same time, and the cartels were supplied with synthetic drugs by a young Valian pharmaceutical company: [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Zyx[/color][/url][color=white].[/color]

[color=white]The war ended in 2021 with the Truce of Tegucigalpa, which turned the largest cartels into legal companies in the states they held. About 210,000 people died, and hundreds of thousands walked north to [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Las Dulces[/color][/url][color=white]. For Valian companies the war set the pattern of the century: ArmaTech learned to sell to both sides, and Zyx, in its first international scandal, learned only to hide better.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE LAGOS INTERVENTION (2027–2029)[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]After losing [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832719][color=#7FDBFF]Hermosa[/color][/url][color=white], its headquarters and its monopoly in 2022, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]WM[/color][/url][color=white] nearly collapsed. It survived abroad. In 2027 [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]BeDay[/color][/url][color=white] hired it to guard its oil platforms in the Niger Delta, where militias had been blowing up pipelines for years. WM landed on Bonny Island that spring, and in 2028 fought the Battle of the Creeks, a year of boat raids in the mangroves.[/color]

[color=white]In 2029 BeDay sold its platforms and WM went home, rich again. About 18,000 people died, 1,400 of them WM contractors. The intervention rebuilt WM as the army for hire it still is — and taught a generation of Africans what Valian corporations do when they come to protect something. Their answer came forty-six years later, in the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832686][color=#7FDBFF]Treaty of Lagos[/color][/url][color=white].[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE STRAIT WAR (2036–2037)[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]When China closed its exports of rare earths, the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832728][color=#7FDBFF]Pacific Union[/color][/url][color=white] blockaded the Strait. Fourteen months of sea battles and network attacks changed no border. Zyx rented the old ArmaTech hackers to both sides at the same time, and after the war the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999866][color=#7FDBFF]Cabinet[/color][/url][color=white] wrote down for the first time the doctrine it still follows: the State stays neutral, and everything else is for sale.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE RENTED ROBOTS WAR (2053–2056)[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]In 2053 armed militias took the Amazon frontier of Brazil. Brazil did not send its own soldiers: it rented whole armies from [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Automa[/color][/url][color=white]. The robots held the Manaus line in 2054, fought a river campaign in 2055 that cost 80,000 machines, and retook the frontier in 2056. About 46,000 people died. It was the first war won by a country that never sent a single soldier.[/color]

[color=white]Brazil paid in food. During the Thirst, when Los Vales could not grow its own grain, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832714][color=#7FDBFF]Cana Viva[/color][/url][color=white] sold it below market price — the trade the country still calls [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832733][color=#7FDBFF]Grain for Robots[/color][/url][color=white]. Brazil also asked for the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832551][color=#7FDBFF]kill code[/color][/url][color=white] of the robots it had paid for. Automa refused.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE KINSHASA REBELLION (2060–2062)[/b][/color][/size]

[url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832714][color=#7FDBFF]RedStar[/color][/url][color=white] owned the cobalt mines of the Congo, and cobalt is in every implant. In 2060 the miners went on strike; in 2061 they took the mine towns with rifles nobody could explain. In 2062 the documents came out: [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Kizuna[/color][/url][color=white] had paid for the rifles, to break RedStar’s hold on the metal inside its own products.[/color]

[color=white]RedStar crushed the rebellion that same year. About 33,000 people died, almost all of them miners, and nobody paid them back. Kizuna has never apologized. RedStar never forgot, and the distrust between the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832727][color=#7FDBFF]Neo-Soviet bloc[/color][/url][color=white] and the Valian companies was one of the sparks of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832555][color=#7FDBFF]World War III[/color][/url][color=white].[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]WORLD WAR III (2067–2073)[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The largest war of the century killed about 39 million people and had no winner. Los Vales sold weapons, robots, space metal, grain and the Rest Front to every army on Earth, lost 64,000 contractors who were never counted as war dead, and came out as the richest country in the world.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[align=center][img]https://thgongarena91-ui.github.io/lv-assets/bpa-wars-abroad/fig-wars-abroad-8.png[/img][/align]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE ORBITAL CONFLICT (2076–2078)[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]In orbit the war was never declared. Satellites went dark, asteroids changed owners overnight and in 2077 a BeDay Astral station exploded with 41 people aboard. 136 people died in two years, all of them in space. The treaty of 2078 divided the asteroid belt and never mentioned the station.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE CRISIS OF THE WALL (2084–TODAY)[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Since 2084 famine inside the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832726][color=#7FDBFF]New American Union[/color][/url][color=white] has pushed millions toward the border, and the Union built a wall to keep them in. Los Vales answered in its own way: [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Lockwell[/color][/url][color=white] opened "work visa" stations along [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832726][color=#7FDBFF]the Wall[/color][/url][color=white] in 2085, and in 2086 [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Cerberus[/color][/url][color=white] hacked the Union’s border system and opened the gates for six hours. Ninety thousand people crossed. Most of them are in the labor camps of the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Escaldar[/color][/url][color=white] today.[/color]

[color=white]About 3,000 people die at the Wall every year. The Union accuses Los Vales of human trafficking; the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Meridian Trust[/color][/url][color=white] answers by freezing American assets abroad. It is the only one of the country’s wars still being fought — and the only one that could still become a real one.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]WHAT IT COSTS[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]No Valian soldier has died abroad, because Los Vales has almost no soldiers. Its dead are WM contractors, Automa machines and the people on the other side. Abroad, Los Vales is known by a name nobody uses at home: [/color][color=white][i]the arms dealer of the West[/i][/color][color=white].[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]
